glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
aokora-mosque.desc: Aokora Mosque stands at a spot called Mirzar Math on the bank of the Belan river, near Pakerhat in Khansama upazila. It was built in 1766 by Mirza Lal Beg. 'Aokora' means 'to speak': people say that anyone talking as they walked past used to hear their words echo back, so locals called it the talking mosque. Time and decay have taken the echo away, and the old building now looks weathered. It is a peaceful, little-visited corner of rural Dinajpur.
blocks: How to get there
From Dinajpur take a bus to Khansama, then an auto or van towards Pakerhat in Angarpara union and ask for Aokora Mosque.
Good to know
Go in daylight and ask at Pakerhat bazar for directions; the lanes are not signposted.

glance: Rice and grocery shops in Dinajpur town's bazar
kataribhog-rice.desc: Kataribhog is an aromatic, long-grained rice variety strongly associated with Dinajpur. Cooked, it is soft and fragrant, making it a favourite for polao, khichuri and festive payesh. Dinajpur's Kataribhog chira (flattened rice) is also widely sought, eaten with doi, gur or bananas. Many visitors take a bag home from the town's rice shops.
blocks: Good to know
New-harvest rice after the Aman season is the most fragrant.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
kantajew-temple.desc: Completed in 1752 by Maharaja Ramnath of Dinajpur, Kantajew Temple is dedicated to Krishna. Its three-storey brick body is covered with thousands of terracotta plaques showing scenes from the Mahabharata and Ramayana, Krishna's life and everyday 18th-century life, from hunts to processions. The nine spires that once crowned it fell in an earthquake in 1897, but the decoration survives remarkably well. It stands beside the Dhepa River in the village of Kantanagar.
blocks: How to get there
About 20 km north of Dinajpur town in Kaharol upazila; take a bus or CNG along the Dinajpur–Thakurgaon road and turn off at Kantanagar.
Good to know
Bring binoculars or a zoom lens to read the upper panels. Go in the morning for the best light.

kantajew-rash-mela.desc: Every year around the full moon of Rash Purnima, devotees gather at Kantajew Temple for the Rash festival celebrating Krishna. The fields around the temple fill with a long-running fair, with stalls of sweets, toys, furniture, pottery and household goods. Pilgrims come from across North Bengal and beyond, and there is music and devotional activity. It is the best time to see the temple as a living place of worship.
blocks: How to get there
As for Kantajew Temple; transport is busier during the fair.
Good to know
Dates follow the lunar calendar, usually in November. Expect heavy crowds.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
dinajpur-museum.desc: Dinajpur Museum, in the Munshipara area of the town, was founded in 1968 by A.K.M. Zakaria, the official who also uncovered Sitakot Vihara. He travelled the villages of greater Dinajpur, Rangpur and Bogura collecting stone and bronze images, coins and inscriptions, and local people donated more. Its collection of antiquities is counted among the largest in the country outside Dhaka. It is a good stop before or after visiting Kantajew Temple and the region's ruins, which many of its objects came from.
blocks: How to get there
In Dinajpur town, take a rickshaw to Munshipara.
Good to know
Check opening days locally before you go, as small museums often close one day a week.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
dinajpur-rajbari.desc: The Dinajpur Raj family, patrons of Kantajew and Ramsagar, lived in this large palace complex on the north-east edge of town. Much of the palace is in ruins, but gateways, walls and parts of the main buildings remain, along with a Krishna temple and other shrines that still see worship. Ponds and trees fill the compound. It helps to connect the story of the family that shaped Dinajpur's heritage.
blocks: How to get there
A short rickshaw ride from Dinajpur town centre.
Good to know
Parts are unstable; stay out of damaged buildings.

glance: About 150–250 BDT per kg depending on the lentil
Papad shops and workshops in Chawkbazar, Dinajpur town
dinajpur-papad.desc: Dinajpur is the papad capital of Bangladesh. In the lanes of Chawkbazar, Notunpara, Basuniapatti, Churipatti, Rajbari and other neighbourhoods, women roll out mung, khesari or mashkalai dough flavoured with cumin, black cumin, chilli and asafoetida into paper-thin rounds and dry them in the sun. Tens of thousands of people earn from it. Fried in hot oil, a papad puffs up in seconds and goes with khichuri or dal-bhat, or is eaten on its own as a snack.
blocks: Good to know
Mung papad costs a bit more but is the classic one to buy.

glance: Sold by the hundred; roughly 300–700 BDT per 100 depending on variety
Litchi markets in Dinajpur town and orchards around Masimpur in late May–June
dinajpur-litchi.desc: For a few weeks each summer, Dinajpur's orchards are heavy with red fruit, and the town fills with traders. The best-known varieties include Bedana, with its tiny seed and abundant flesh, and the large China-3, alongside Bombai and Madrajie. The Masimpur area near town is especially famous for its trees. Eating fresh litchi in Dinajpur during the season is a summer pleasure.
blocks: Good to know
Bedana and China-3 are the premium varieties and ripen later than Madrajie.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
nawabganj-national-park.desc: Locals call it the Nawabganj Shal Bagan. The forest starts about a kilometre north-west of Nawabganj upazila town and covers some 517 hectares, declared a national park in 2010. Sal and teak dominate, with gamari, jam and acacia, and orchids on some trunks. Jungle cats, fishing cats, foxes and many birds live here, though you are more likely to hear than see them. Combined with Swapnapuri and Sitakot Vihara, it makes an easy day in the upazila.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus from Dinajpur to Nawabganj upazila town; the forest begins about 1 km away, reachable on foot or by van.
Good to know
Morning walks are best for birds. Stick to the main tracks.

nayabad-mosque.desc: Nayabad Mosque stands in a village not far from Kantajew Temple and dates from the late 18th century. Local tradition says it was built for Muslim artisans who came to work on the temple. The small brick mosque has three domes and terracotta panels on its facade, many worn but still graceful. It is easy to combine with Kantajew, yet few visitors make the detour.
blocks: How to get there
From Kantanagar, take a rickshaw or van along village roads; ask for Nayabad.
Good to know
Dress modestly and visit outside prayer times.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
ramsagar.desc: Ramsagar was dug in the 18th century under Raja Ram Nath and is among the largest man-made ponds in Bangladesh, stretching for about a kilometre. Its banks are planted with trees and paths, and the area is protected as a national park. A small deer enclosure and resting spots make it popular with families. On quiet mornings the water is still and the birds are easy to spot.
blocks: How to get there
About 8 km south of Dinajpur town; take an auto-rickshaw or CNG.
Good to know
Weekday mornings are quietest. Do not feed the animals.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
singra-national-park.desc: Known locally as Singra Shalban, this protected sal forest lies in Bhognagar union of Birganj upazila, about 40 km north of Dinajpur town. About 305 hectares were declared a national park in 2010. The small Norto river winds through the forest, and paths lead between tall, straight sal trunks. There is a small rest house and two picnic spots, and visitor numbers climb in the winter months. Otherwise it is mostly birdsong and the crunch of dry leaves.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus from Dinajpur towards Birganj on the Thakurgaon highway, then an auto or van to the forest in Bhognagar union (about 15 km from Birganj).
Good to know
Go in daylight and in a group; the forest is quiet and lightly staffed. Take your rubbish back with you.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
sitakot-vihara.desc: Local legend held that Sita spent her second exile here, and colonial gazetteers took the mound for a walled pond. In 1968 and 1972–73 excavations uncovered a square Buddhist monastery about 65 metres a side, with 41 cells around a central courtyard and an entrance on the north. Bronze images of the Bodhisattvas Padmapani and Manjushri, terracotta toys and ornamental bricks were found. It belongs to the same broad era as Paharpur and Halud Vihara. The site is protected but sees few visitors, and the low brick walls sit quietly among village fields.
blocks: How to get there
From Nawabganj upazila town (bus from Dinajpur), take an auto or van to Sitakot in the Fatepur Marash area.
Good to know
There are no facilities; bring water. Combine with Nawabganj National Park and Swapnapuri.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
sura-mosque.desc: Sura Mosque, also called Shuja Mosque, stands beside an ancient pond on the Ghoraghat–Hili road, about 10 km west of Ghoraghat upazila. It is a protected monument of the Department of Archaeology. The building has a single-domed prayer hall with a verandah topped by three small domes, and corner towers made of black stone. Inside, the mihrabs carry fine carved decoration, and granite and other stones are worked into the walls. Its compact size and setting by the water make it one of the most attractive old mosques in the north.
blocks: How to get there
From Dinajpur take a bus to Ghoraghat, then an auto 10 km west along the Hili road.
Good to know
It is an active mosque; dress modestly and avoid prayer times. Ghoraghat Fort ruins are nearby for history lovers.

glance: 335 km to Dinajpur by road, 9–11 hours by bus or car
Ticketed entry; rides and some sections charged separately
swapnapuri-amusement-park.desc: Swapnapuri, at Aftabganj in Nawabganj upazila, is one of the best-known picnic spots in northern Bangladesh. Spread over a large area, it has rides, artificial lakes, gardens and a small zoo, along with rest houses and a central picnic ground. Odd attractions include the 'Fish World' aquarium of model sea creatures, an animal kingdom of giant sculptures from flamingos to dinosaurs, and an art gallery. In the winter picnic season buses of students and office groups fill the car park.
blocks: How to get there
From Dinajpur town take a bus or hired microbus/CNG towards Nawabganj and Aftabganj; Nawabganj National Park and Sitakot Vihara are in the same upazila.
Good to know
Weekdays outside December–January are much calmer. Rest houses inside can be booked for a night.
